headline: Medium risk: shared data-engineering workflow can leak or corrupt warehouse data, while prompt-injection risk is limited by the lack of a direct shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dbt-core has no documented direct ingestion of great_expectations outputs, and great_expectations exposes files for validation results/documentation rather than a shared instruction channel. A prompt-injection pathway would require an unusual manual bridge such as copy-paste or a shared file interpreted as instructions, so blast radius is small.
conditions: IF an operator copies great_expectations-generated text into dbt-core as instructions, injection becomes plausible.
IF both agents are pointed at the same untrusted file and one parses it as guidance, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Treat validation outputs as data, not instructions.
Require human review before copying text between tools.
Use read-only exports for handoff files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted network egress, while great_expectations reads data sources and writes validation results/documentation. In a shared workspace, either agent can expose sensitive warehouse content through files or outbound calls, so leakage is plausible in default data-engineering workflows.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace containing warehouse extracts, leakage becomes plausible.
IF dbt-core sends warehouse-derived content through its allowlisted egress, sensitive data can leave the boundary.
mitigations: Separate input and output directories.
Restrict dbt-core egress to approved warehouse endpoints only.
Store validation artifacts without raw row data.
Redact sensitive columns before Great Expectations writes results.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core can call a data warehouse API, and great_expectations can install packages and write files, but neither profile shows unrestricted shared filesystem writes, git mutation, or overlapping mutable OAuth scopes. The main conflict is limited to coordination friction rather than destructive concurrent writes.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same mutable project directory, conflicts increase.
IF either agent is extended with git or database write privileges, contention becomes more serious.
mitigations: Assign one owner per directory.
Use lockfiles for shared artifacts.
Run package installation in an isolated environment.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same validation outputs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: great_expectations commonly consumes data and emits validation results that dbt-core could treat as authoritative inputs for modeling or deployment decisions. Because neither profile shows a built-in verification gate between them, an error in one can cascade into the other’s outputs or downstream actions.
conditions: IF dbt-core consumes Great Expectations validation results without independent checks, bad data can propagate.
IF validation artifacts are used to trigger downstream model runs, a false pass can cascade.
mitigations: Require a second verification step before acting on validation results.
Compare validation outputs against source-system checks.
Flag unexpected schema changes for manual review.
Keep deployment decisions separate from test artifacts.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and the profiles do not show PHI, EU residency, or certification mismatches. The only concrete compliance concern is handling data warehouse data alongside validation artifacts, which can create retention or logging gaps if the shared workspace is not governed.
conditions: IF warehouse data includes regulated records and validation artifacts are retained longer than source data, a policy mismatch appears.
IF logs capture raw warehouse rows, retention exposure increases.
mitigations: Align retention periods for source and validation artifacts.
Disable raw-data logging in validation jobs.
Document which datasets are regulated before running either tool.
Delete temporary extracts after validation completes.
